answer.evidence: The bed is drawn from straight above. The soil ridges run as horizontal stripes inside a uniform-width plank frame. The south plank (rows 46-47) is only a 2-row lip with a dark underside row at 47. It has no front face of 3 or more rows, no eave line or shadow, and no receding side face. The plants are small decor. The sprite sits on a full 80x64 dirt-ground tile, and the bed occupies rows ~15-48.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are acceptable: 5 visible tones per tile (grass reference 3, paving reference 7), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted brown rather than black. The weakness is in the shading ramps. The whole patch uses only 13 distinct colours across the soil, plank frame and bean plants, so each material gets about 3 steps against the references' 5-6. The plank frame reads thin and flat, with a single lit edge and a dark edge rather than a thick weathered plank with grain, joint detail and broken overlapping corners. The leaves are small dots in 2-3 greens with little clump structure. The soil ridges and surrounding dirt carry only light speckle, and the ridge tones do not model the rows. Next to the paving reference, which is shaded stone by stone, this reads as a simpler, thinner and flatter piece. It is not a sticker or a flat fill, but the shading is too shallow to pass.
